sections.h2: Where is Eastchester, and which communities sit inside it?
sections.html:
Eastchester is a town in southern Westchester County, roughly 5 miles south of White Plains and 20 miles north of New York City, according to the town's local snapshot. It has about 4.87 square miles of land and a 2020 population of 34,641, which works out to more than 7,100 people per square mile. Scarsdale lies to the north, New Rochelle to the east, Yonkers to the west and Mount Vernon to the south.

Two incorporated villages, Bronxville and Tuckahoe, sit inside the town boundaries. The remainder is the unincorporated area also called Eastchester, with neighborhoods such as Lake Isle, Twin Lakes, California Ridge, Hickory Hills, Huntley Estates, Chester Heights, Garth Road and Waverly Heights. Whether a house is in a village or in the unincorporated part decides which local offices serve it, so confirm that first. Most town offices share Town Hall at 40 Mill Road, which was dedicated in 1957 on the site of a former country club.

sections.h2: How old is Eastchester, and what is its history?
sections.html:
Ten families from Fairfield, Connecticut settled the area in 1664, and a 1665 agreement called the Eastchester Covenant set its laws with 26 provisions covering schooling, property upkeep and support of a minister. A second patent from Queen Anne followed in 1708. The town sat in the Neutral Ground during the Revolution, and the village green hosted a contested 1733 election that figured in the John Peter Zenger libel case.

Railroads in the 1840s ended the farming era. Bronxville was incorporated as a village in 1898 and Tuckahoe in 1903. Quarries opened in 1821 produced the Tuckahoe marble used in buildings such as the Government Printing Office in Washington and St. Patrick's Cathedral. Eastchester High School was finished in 1927, and the one-room Marble Schoolhouse of 1835 still stands on California Road.

sections.h2: How do Eastchester's homeowners look in federal data?
sections.html:
QuickFacts shows 34,015 residents for mid-2025, which is 1.8 percent below its 2020 base. The detailed figures are in its QuickFacts profile.

  • Homes occupied by their owners: 72.3 percent
  • Typical owner-occupied home value (2020 to 2024): $806,300
  • Typical household income: $155,726
  • Typical monthly rent: $2,302
  • Adults with a bachelor's degree or higher: 68.0 percent
  • Average trip to work: 35.9 minutes

The survey lists monthly owner costs with a mortgage as $4,000 or more, and costs without a mortgage as $1,500 or more.

sections.h2: How do trains, parkways and schools affect an Eastchester sale?
sections.html:
Metro-North's Harlem Line stops at Crestwood, Tuckahoe and Bronxville, and the town sits between the Hutchinson River and Bronx River Parkways, with Route 22 running through the middle. Lawrence Hospital is in Bronxville. Rail and parkway access is easy to verify, so give a buyer the walking distance to a station instead of a general claim.

Three school systems cover the town: the Eastchester Union Free School District, the Tuckahoe School District and the Bronxville Schools. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects the Eastchester and Tuckahoe district taxes. For a Bronxville Schools address, ask that district how its taxes are billed. Name the district in any listing.

sections.h2: When are Eastchester property taxes due?
sections.html:
County and town taxes are paid once a year and are due without penalty by April 30. School taxes follow a July 1 to June 30 fiscal year and are paid in two halves. The Receiver of Taxes also handles notices of tax lien sales and gives callers information on apportioning taxes in a real estate sale.

Source: Town of Eastchester Receiver of Taxes FAQ. The 2026-2027 first-half school bills were mailed ahead of the September 30 deadline, so the January 31 second-half payment is the next school date.

sections.h2: What can the Eastchester Assessor tell a seller?
sections.html:
The Assessor estimates market value by comparing recent sales, by replacement cost, or, for rental property, by income. The first of those compares a property with similar homes that sold recently, and state law calls for every property in a town to be assessed at the same percentage of value.

Owners planning an addition or renovation can ask for a written estimate of how it would change the assessment. The request must be in writing, with drawings that mark what exists and what is new, a square footage breakdown, a narrative description and a cost estimate at market prices, even if the owner will do some of the work personally. Estimates usually arrive within a week.

Applications for senior, veterans, STAR and disability exemptions are due to the Assessor by June 1, and residency proof is specific to Eastchester, so ask the office for its forms.

sections.h2: What permit and zoning steps can slow an Eastchester house sale?
sections.html:
The Zoning Law requires many development applications to win Planning Board approval before a building permit can even be requested. Some also need review by the Architectural Review Board, the Zoning Board of Appeals if a variance or special permit is involved, or the Sign Review Board. The Planning Department staffs all four and works from Town Hall at 40 Mill Road, Room 216.

  • Comments on a hearing item must reach the Secretary to the Land Use Boards by 4:00 pm on the business day before the meeting, or be handed to the board at the hearing.
  • The Building Department, also in Room 216, takes building permit applications.
  • Town Hall is open Monday to Friday, 8:30 am to 4:30 pm.

Before listing, find out whether any past addition or sign went through the right board, because a buyer's attorney may ask to see those approvals.

sections.h2: Which state transfer rules touch an Eastchester closing?
sections.html: New York State charges $2 for every $500 of consideration on a conveyance, and the TP-584 return is filed with the county clerk where the property lies. Residences priced at $1 million or more also trigger a 1 percent charge that the buyer pays under the state's transfer tax rules.

sections.h2: How can an Eastchester owner sell quickly?
sections.html:
Options include a broker listing, a sale handled by the owner, and a purchase by a cash buyer. Cash is often the shortest path when a house needs work or the owner needs a firm closing date, and the offer usually lands below what a market sale could bring.

Before choosing, request the tax status from the Receiver of Taxes, check permits with the Building Department, and decide which school district and village the house belongs to. Those answers shape both price and timing.

faqs.q: Are Bronxville and Tuckahoe part of Eastchester?
faqs.a: Yes, both are incorporated villages located inside the Town of Eastchester. The town also includes an unincorporated area that the Census Bureau treats as the Eastchester census-designated place.

faqs.q: What is a typical Eastchester house worth?
faqs.a: Around $806,300 for homes lived in by their owners, based on the Census Bureau's 2020 to 2024 survey. Household income in the middle of the range is $155,726.

faqs.q: When are school taxes due in Eastchester?
faqs.a: September 30 is the cutoff for the first half and January 31 for the second, both without penalty. The town's Receiver of Taxes collects for both the Eastchester and Tuckahoe districts.

faqs.q: What happens if Eastchester county and town taxes are paid late?
faqs.a: The cost rises with each month. May adds 2 percent, June and July 5 percent, August and September 7 percent, and the final quarter of the year 10 percent, with no charge through April 30.

faqs.q: Which office takes Eastchester exemption forms?
faqs.a: The Assessor's Office at Town Hall, 40 Mill Road. Its FAQ gives June 1 as the deadline for exemption applications, and applicants must show Eastchester residency.
